title: ECC/NVLink composite case & runbook draft: power-ripple induced link training flaps
body:
TL;DR:
We observed a cluster of intermittent GPU node instability events across three racks over a 48-hour window (2026-07-13 to 2026-07-14). Symptoms: bursts of correctable ECC errors followed, within minutes, by NVLink link training failures and then driver hang/crash on affected nodes. Root hypothesis under investigation: correlated power-rail ripple (PSU/transient) during high-concurrency p2p workloads increases ECC correctable rates which impacts NVLink training state machine, causing asymmetric link negotiation and eventual driver OOM/hang.

Why this doc exists (context):
- Quick summary for oncall handoff and runbook draft to reduce MTTR for similar future waves.
- Capture reproducible microbench and mitigation checklist we used in the field.
- Collect data + telemetry gaps for longer-term fixes (firmware/driver/infra).

Incident timeline (abridged):
- 2026-07-13 01:12 UTC: Alert - spike in correctable ECC by 2x baseline on rack-7 nodes (alert CON-8742).
- 2026-07-13 01:18 UTC: First job eviction (k8s) on node gpu-r7c2 after kernel Oops observed.
- 2026-07-13 01:22 UTC: NVLink training failures logged (link training retry, asymmetric lanes).
- 2026-07-13 01:30 UTC: Driver process crash (nvidia) with backtrace referencing nvlink and mmu ops.
- 2026-07-13 02:05 UTC: Repeat in rack-8 nodes under similar mixed p2p workload.
- 2026-07-14 11:40 UTC: Nightshift SRE reproduced ECC surge by injecting synthetic allreduce workload with staged p2p fanout.

Field evidence collected:
- dmesg excerpts (saved in linked tar): repeated nvlink negotiation failures, timestamps align with ECC correctable counters.
- GPU health telemetry (gpubus/metrics): rapid rise in correctable ECC, short plateau, then link retransmit counts up.
- PSU telemetry (BMC): small transient voltage droops (~0.7-1.2% under peak) coincident with ECC spikes on two nodes (gpu-r7c2, gpu-r8c1).
- Kernel oops/backtrace: references to lru/kvm mappings and nvidia_kvm_mm faults in the driver path.

Hypothesis (working):
- High-concurrency p2p operations create bursts in memory/IO activity causing localized switching noise. Small PSU voltage ripples -> increases ECC-correctable events -> NVLink training state machines see inconsistent symbol errors -> link training restarts or asymmetric channel activation -> driver more likely to hit recovery/hung state (especially if paired with heavy kvcache pressure).
- This is not a pure silicon hardware fault; it is a compound reliability issue at the infra+driver boundary.

How we reproduced (microbench):
1) On isolated node, run a staged allreduce + random large tensor transfers with two simultaneous kernels pinned to different SM islands.
2) Use our p2p-fanout tool (github link in artifacts) to create progressive fanout until ECC correctables spike.
3) Monitor: nvlink_link_errors, ecc_correctable_count, driver_uptime.
4) On repro runs we saw training retries and eventual driver recovery timeouts in ~10–25 minutes.

Immediate mitigations applied (hotfixes):
- Shifted high-fanout p2p workloads to nodes with matching PSU vendor (reduced incident surface).
- Short-term k8s policy: set nodeSelector to avoid oversubscribing NVLink topologies; add pod anti-affinity for large p2p jobs.
- Increased ECC scrub frequency (where supported by driver) to reduce transient correctable accumulation.
- Emergency kube drain/cordon and cold-reboot on node if NVLink training loops > 3 in 15m.
- Rolled back a recent driver candidate on a canary pool (candidate had new mmu path) — reduced crash rate on canary.

Draft runbook (for oncall SREs) - quick steps (concise):
1) Initial triage: check cluster telemetry dashboard for ECC spikes and nvlink training count. Look for pattern across nodes in same rack/backplane.
2) If ECC correctable rate > baseline * 2 and nvlink_training_retries > 5: set alert level -> escalate to eng-sre and applied-ml.
3) Triage commands to run (collect quickly):
   - sudo dmesg --since "15 minutes" | grep -i nvlink
   - nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.corrected.volatile --format=csv -a
   - /opt/redwood/bin/collect-gpu-health --since 30m --output /tmp/gpu-collect-$(date +%s).tgz
   - ipmitool sensor list | grep -i volt
4) If driver's kernel oops present: capture /var/crash, call for immediate node drain.
5) If reproduced on multiple nodes in rack -> suspect PSU/backplane ripple -> engage infra (hardware-oncall) to check BMC/PSU logs and switch PDUs to alternate feed if available.
6) For immediate customer-facing mitigation: move latency-sensitive calls to dedicated non-p2p pool and announce degraded GPU capacity with ETA.

Recovery checklist (post-fix verification):
- Confirm ECC correctable counters returning to baseline after reboot (30–60m observation).
- NVLink training stable for 1 hour under light p2p smoke test.
- No kernel oops in dmesg for 24 hours.

Longer-term fixes under evaluation:
- Firmware: push PSU/BMC logging aggregation improvement and enable higher frequency sampling on suspect racks.
- Driver: engage upstream vendor to investigate training state machine hardening when correctable bursts occur. Patch candidate: add backoff/recovery window for training that tolerates short ECC spikes.
- Kernel/OS: reduce kernel-level kvcache pressure by tuning oom/kvm thresholds for driver memory paths.
- Infra: replace suspect PDUs and validate that PDU cross-feed parity eliminates correlated droops.

Telemetry & alerting changes proposed:
- New composite alert: ECC_correctable_rate * NVLink_retry_count > threshold -> page oncall (currently separate alerts were noisy and missed joint pattern).
- Add PDU/BMC metrics ingestion into GPU health dashboard (sample at 10s for high-sensitivity racks).
- Add synthetic p2p smoke probe run every 4 hours on representative nodes to detect training instability before customer impact.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why does the driver crash on some nodes and not others with similar ECC spikes? Hardware variation (PSU vendor, board revision) suspected. Need BOM correlation.
- Are certain models/firmware combos more tolerant? We need to build matrix across model/firmware/driver versions.
- Does memory temperature correlate? Our thermal telemetry shows only minor temp bumps but need higher-res sampling.

Next actions (owners + rough ETA):
- Collect BOM and PDU mapping for rack-7/8 (owner: Marco Li) — ETA 2026-07-20.
- Create a small canary fleet with alternate PSU vendor and run long-running p2p stress (owner: Ellen Park) — ETA 2026-07-25.
- File upstream vendor bug with crash backtraces and reduced repro (owner: Josef Müller) — ETA 2026-07-19.
- Implement composite alert and 10s PDU ingestion prototype (owner: Ravi Patel) — ETA 2026-07-22.

Notes to self / informal fragments we recorded during the run:
- "felt like link training was getting flapped by noise rather than permanent lane failure"
- keep capture size small (10–20MB of dmesg + nvlink counters) for fast uploads during oncall.
- possible low-effort mitigation: stagger p2p job start times (fanout ramp) to avoid simultaneous corner-case state.

Appendix (snippets):
- sample dmesg line: "[1628778123.345678] nvlink: link training retry 4 on link 2 (asymmetric lanes)"
- nvidia-smi excerpt: "ecc.corrected.volatile, gpu-0: 124 -> 874 in 12m"
- sample driver OOPS header: stable: "BUG: unable to handle kernel NULL pointer dereference at 00000000ffffffff" followed by stack trace with modules: nvidia, nvlink, nvswitch

If you're reading this as the next responder: add anything we missed to the 'Next actions' block and mark status -> in_review -> final once we've validated canary results.

-- Aisha (oncall lead 2026-07-14)
